title: Targeting p53-MDM2 interactions to identify small molecule inhibitors for cancer therapy: beyond "Failure to rescue".
authors: Chukwuemeka, Prosper Obed; Umar, Haruna Isiyaku; Iwaloye, Opeyemi; Oretade, Oluwaseyi Matthew; Olowosoke, Christopher Busayo; Elabiyi, Michael Omoniyi; Igbe, Festus Omotere; Oretade, Oyeyemi Janet; Eigbe, Joy Oseme; Adeojo, Funmilayo Janet
one_liner_zh: 该文聚焦p53-MDM2蛋白-蛋白互作的小分子抑制剂筛选，虽用虚拟筛选、对接和MD模拟，但对象为蛋白-蛋白而非蛋白-DNA互作，与本课题TF-DNA结合机制无关。
abstract: At present, disrupting p53-MDM2 interactions through small molecule ligands is a promising approach to safe treatment and management of human cancer. Tumor cells unlike the normal cells, are rapidly evolving affecting the efficacy of many approved anti-cancer agents due to drug resistance. Therefore, identifying a potential anticancer compound is crucial. Pharmacophore based virtual screening, followed by molecular docking, ADMET evaluation, and molecular dynamics studies against MDM2 protein was investigated to identify potential ligands that may act as inhibitors. The model (AHRR_1) with survival score (4.176) was selected among the top ranked generated Pharmacophore hypothesis. Validation of the model hypothesis by an external dataset of actives and inactive compounds produced significant validation attributes including; AUC = 0.85, BEDROC = 0.56 at alpha = 20.0, RIE = 8.18, AUAC = 0.88, and EF of 6.2 at the top 2% of the dataset. The model was use for screening the ZINC database, and the top 1375 hits satisfying the model hypothesis were subjected to molecular docking studies to understand the molecular and structural basis of selectivity of compounds for MDM2 protein. A sub-set of 25 compounds with binding energy lower than the reference inhibitors were evaluated for pharmacokinetic properties. Four compounds (ZINC02639178, ZINC06752762, ZINC38933175, and ZINC77969611) showed the most desired pharmacokinetic profile. Lastly, investigation of the dynamic behaviour of leads-protein complexes through MD simulation showed similar RMSD, RMSF, and H-bond occupancy profile compared to a reference inhibitor, suggesting stability throughout the simulation time. However, ZINC02639178 was found to satisfy the molecular enumeration the most compared to the other three leads. It may emerge as potential treatment option after extensive experimental studies. Communicated by Ramaswamy H. Sarma.
abstract_zh: 目前，通过小分子配体干扰p53-MDM2相互作用是安全治疗和管理人类癌症的一种有前景的方法。与正常细胞不同，肿瘤细胞快速进化，由于耐药性，影响了许多已批准抗癌药物的疗效。因此，识别潜在的抗癌化合物至关重要。本研究采用基于药效团的虚拟筛选，随后进行分子对接、ADMET评估和针对MDM2蛋白的分子动力学研究，以识别可能作为抑制剂的潜在配体。在排名靠前的生成药效团假设中，选择了具有生存评分（4.176）的模型（AHRR_1）。通过外部活性及非活性化合物数据集验证模型假设，产生了显著的验证属性，包括：AUC = 0.85，BEDROC = 0.56（alpha = 20.0），RIE = 8.18，AUAC = 0.88，以及数据集前2%的EF为6.2。该模型用于筛选ZINC数据库，并将满足模型假设的前1375个命中化合物进行分子对接研究，以理解化合物对MDM2蛋白选择性的分子和结构基础。对结合能低于参考抑制剂的25个化合物子集进行了药代动力学特性评估。四个化合物（ZINC02639178、ZINC06752762、ZINC38933175和ZINC77969611）显示出最理想的药代动力学特征。最后，通过MD模拟研究先导化合物-蛋白复合物的动态行为，结果显示与参考抑制剂相比，具有相似的RMSD、RMSF和氢键占据率特征，表明在整个模拟时间内具有稳定性。然而，发现ZINC02639178在分子枚举方面比其他三个先导化合物更满足要求。经过广泛的实验研究后，它可能成为潜在的治疗选择。由Ramaswamy H. Sarma通讯。
